8. Post-condition: the condition that the system and the output must satisfy after the operation is executed.

# Requirement
```text
Airlines offer different flights. Each flight has its unique id. A flight is open for booking and closed by order of the company. A customer can book one or more flights, for different passengers. A reservation concerns a single flight and a single passenger, has a unique id. A reservation can be confirmed or canceled. A flight has a departure airport and an arrival airport. Each airport has its unique id. A flight has a day and time of departure, and a day and time of arrival (e.g. 2024-12-08 13:00:00). A flight may include stopovers in one or more airport(s). A stopover has a departure time and an arrival time. Each airport serves one or more cities.
Functional requirement:
1.Publish a flight for booking. An airline can publish a newly created flight to make it available for customer bookings. The system first confirms that the flight has valid departure and arrival timestamps in yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss format, then checks temporal consistency — currentTime < departureTime < arrivalTime — and route integrity — departureAirport ≠ arrivalAirport. A flight may be published only once, and before publishing, the flight's openForBooking status must be false. The call returns true on success; otherwise, false.
2.Create a booking for passengers on a flight. A customer selects a specific open flight and supplies a list of passengers names. The system checks that there are no duplicate passengers on the flight and the current time is before the flight departure time. It then generates a booking for the customer and creates a reservation with a unique ID for each passenger in that booking. Each reservation is initially placed in "pending" status until the customer confirms it. The call returns true on success; otherwise, false.
3.Confirm or cancel an existing reservation in a booking. The system checks that the flight has not yet departed and is still open for booking. The customer can then confirm or cancel a reservation by providing its reservation ID. The call returns true on success; otherwise, false.
4.Close an open flight. An airline can close an existing flight that has not yet departed. The system verifies that the flight is currently open; if so, it changes the status to closed and cancels every confirmed reservation. Closing is not allowed on the same calendar day as the flight's departure — even if the current time is before the departure time. It returns true on success; otherwise, false.
5.Retrieve all confirmed reservations for a specific flight. Given a flight object, the system retrieves every confirmed reservation on that flight, provided the flight is currently open for booking. It returns a list of reservations, or empty list if none exist.
```

```plantuml
@startuml

title flights Model

class Airline {
    flights : List<Flight>
    addFlight(f : Flight) : void
    closeFlight(flightId : String, now : EDate) : boolean
    publishFlight(f : Flight, now : EDate) : boolean
    removeFlight(f : Flight) : void
    searchFlights(origin : String, dest : String, date : EDate) : List<Flight>
}
class Airport {
    id : String
    servesForCities : List<City>
    addCity(c : City) : void
}
class Booking {
    customer : Customer
    reservations : List<Reservation>
    createReservation(f : Flight, passenger : String, now : EDate) : boolean
}
class City {
}
class Customer {
    bookings : List<Booking>
    addBooking(f : Flight, now : EDate, listOfPassengerNames : List<String>) : boolean
    cancel(reservationID : String, now : EDate) : boolean
    confirm(reservationID : String, now : EDate) : boolean
}
class Flight {
    arrivalTime : EDate
    departureTime : EDate
    id : String
    openForBooking : boolean
    arrivalAirport : Airport
    departureAirport : Airport
    reservations : List<Reservation>
    stopovers : List<Stopover>
    addStopover(stop : Stopover, now : EDate) : boolean
    getConfirmedReservations() : List<Reservation>
    removeStopover(stop : Stopover, now : EDate) : boolean
}
class Passenger {
    name : String
}
class Reservation {
    id : String
    status : ReservationStatus
    flight : Flight
    passenger : Passenger
}
class Stopover {
    arrivalTime : EDate
    departureTime : EDate
    airport : Airport
}
enum ReservationStatus {
    PENDING
    CONFIRMED
    CANCELED
}

Airline *-- "*" Flight : flights
Airport --> "*" City : servesForCities
Booking --> Customer : customer
Booking *-- "*" Reservation : reservations
Customer --> "*" Booking : bookings
Flight --> Airport : arrivalAirport
Flight --> Airport : departureAirport
Flight --> "*" Reservation : reservations  'opposite: flight
Flight *-- "*" Stopover : stopovers
Reservation --> Flight : flight  'opposite: reservations
Reservation --> Passenger : passenger
Stopover --> Airport : airport
@enduml
```

# Requirement
```text
Airlines offer different flights. Each flight has its unique id. A flight is open for booking and closed by order of the company. A customer can book one or more flights, for different passengers. A reservation concerns a single flight and a single passenger, has a unique id. A reservation can be confirmed or canceled. A flight has a departure airport and an arrival airport. Each airport has its unique id. A flight has a day and time of departure, and a day and time of arrival (e.g. 2024-12-08 13:00:00). A flight may include stopovers in one or more airport(s). A stopover has a departure time and an arrival time. Each airport serves one or more cities.
Functional requirement:
1.Publish a flight for booking. An airline can publish a newly created flight to make it available for customer bookings. The system first confirms that the flight has valid departure and arrival timestamps in yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss format, then checks temporal consistency — currentTime < departureTime < arrivalTime — and route integrity — departureAirport ≠ arrivalAirport. A flight may be published only once, and before publishing, the flight's openForBooking status must be false. The call returns true on success; otherwise, false.
2.Create a booking for passengers on a flight. A customer selects a specific open flight and supplies a list of passengers names. The system checks that there are no duplicate passengers on the flight and the current time is before the flight departure time. It then generates a booking for the customer and creates a reservation with a unique ID for each passenger in that booking. Each reservation is initially placed in "pending" status until the customer confirms it. The call returns true on success; otherwise, false.
3.Confirm or cancel an existing reservation in a booking. The system checks that the flight has not yet departed and is still open for booking. The customer can then confirm or cancel a reservation by providing its reservation ID. The call returns true on success; otherwise, false.
4.Close an open flight. An airline can close an existing flight that has not yet departed. The system verifies that the flight is currently open; if so, it changes the status to closed and cancels every confirmed reservation. Closing is not allowed on the same calendar day as the flight's departure — even if the current time is before the departure time. It returns true on success; otherwise, false.
5.Retrieve all confirmed reservations for a specific flight. Given a flight object, the system retrieves every confirmed reservation on that flight, provided the flight is currently open for booking. It returns a list of reservations, or empty list if none exist.
```

Each airport has its unique id. A flight has a day and time of departure, and a day and time of arrival (e.g. 2024-12-08 13:00:00). A flight may include stopovers in one or more airport(s). A stopover has a departure time and an arrival time. Each airport serves one or more cities.
```text
Functional requirement:
1.Publish a flight for booking. An airline can publish a newly created flight to make it available for customer bookings. The system first confirms that the flight has valid departure and arrival timestamps in yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss format, then checks temporal consistency — currentTime < departureTime < arrivalTime — and route integrity — departureAirport ≠ arrivalAirport. A flight may be published only once, and before publishing, the flight's openForBooking status must be false. The call returns true on success; otherwise, false.
2.Create a booking for passengers on a flight. A customer selects a specific open flight and supplies a list of passengers names. The system checks that there are no duplicate passengers on the flight and the current time is before the flight departure time. It then generates a booking for the customer and creates a reservation with a unique ID for each passenger in that booking. Each reservation is initially placed in "pending" status until the customer confirms it. The call returns true on success; otherwise, false.
3.Confirm or cancel an existing reservation in a booking. The system checks that the flight has not yet departed and is still open for booking. The customer can then confirm or cancel a reservation by providing its reservation ID. The call returns true on success; otherwise, false.
4.Close an open flight. An airline can close an existing flight that has not yet departed. The system verifies that the flight is currently open; if so, it changes the status to closed and cancels every confirmed reservation. Closing is not allowed on the same calendar day as the flight's departure — even if the current time is before the departure time. It returns true on success; otherwise, false.
5.Retrieve all confirmed reservations for a specific flight. Given a flight object, the system retrieves every confirmed reservation on that flight, provided the flight is currently open for booking. It returns a list of reservations, or empty list if none exist.
```

# Requirement
```text
Airlines offer different flights. Each flight has its unique id. A flight is open for booking and closed by order of the company. A customer can book one or more flights, for different passengers. A reservation concerns a single flight and a single passenger, has a unique id. A reservation can be confirmed or canceled. A flight has a departure airport and an arrival airport. Each airport has its unique id. A flight has a day and time of departure, and a day and time of arrival (e.g. 2024-12-08 13:00:00). A flight may include stopovers in one or more airport(s). A stopover has a departure time and an arrival time. Each airport serves one or more cities.
Functional requirement:
1.Publish a flight for booking. An airline can publish a newly created flight to make it available for customer bookings. The system first confirms that the flight has valid departure and arrival timestamps in yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss format, then checks temporal consistency — currentTime < departureTime < arrivalTime — and route integrity — departureAirport ≠ arrivalAirport. A flight may be published only once, and before publishing, the flight's openForBooking status must be false. The call returns true on success; otherwise, false.
2.Create a booking for passengers on a flight. A customer selects a specific open flight and supplies a list of passengers names. The system checks that there are no duplicate passengers on the flight and the current time is before the flight departure time. It then generates a booking for the customer and creates a reservation with a unique ID for each passenger in that booking. Each reservation is initially placed in "pending" status until the customer confirms it. The call returns true on success; otherwise, false.
3.Confirm or cancel an existing reservation in a booking. The system checks that the flight has not yet departed and is still open for booking. The customer can then confirm or cancel a reservation by providing its reservation ID. The call returns true on success; otherwise, false.
4.Close an open flight. An airline can close an existing flight that has not yet departed. The system verifies that the flight is currently open; if so, it changes the status to closed and cancels every confirmed reservation. Closing is not allowed on the same calendar day as the flight's departure — even if the current time is before the departure time. It returns true on success; otherwise, false.
5.Retrieve all confirmed reservations for a specific flight. Given a flight object, the system retrieves every confirmed reservation on that flight, provided the flight is currently open for booking. It returns a list of reservations, or empty list if none exist.
```

Airline::publishFlight
Summary: Makes a flight available for booking.
Algorithm: Validate timestamps: departureTime < arrivalTime and currentTime < departureTime. Ensure departureAirport != arrivalAirport. Check if openForBooking is false. If all pass, set openForBooking to true.
Related Features: flights (List)
Related Classes: Flight, EDate
Input: f (Flight): The flight to publish; now (EDate): Current system date/time.
Output: boolean: true on success, false otherwise.
Pre-condition: Flight exists, openForBooking is false, departureAirport != arrivalAirport, and timestamps are chronologically valid.
Post-condition: Flight status openForBooking is true.

Airline::addFlight
Summary: Adds a new flight instance to the airline's management system.
Algorithm: Check if flight ID is unique within the airline's list; if unique, add the flight object to the flights collection.
Related Features: flights (List)
Related Classes: Flight
Input: f (Flight): The flight object to be added.
Output: void
Pre-condition: Flight f is not null and not already in the list.
Post-condition: The flight f is added to the airline's list of flights.

Airline::closeFlight
Summary: Closes a flight for booking and cancels all confirmed reservations.
Algorithm: Find flight by ID. Check if openForBooking is true and current date is not the same as departure date. If valid, set openForBooking to false, iterate through all reservations, and set status of CONFIRMED reservations to CANCELED.
Related Features: flights (List)
Related Classes: Flight, Reservation, ReservationStatus, EDate
Input: flightId (String): Unique ID of the flight; now (EDate): Current system date/time.
Output: boolean: true if successful, false otherwise.
Pre-condition: Flight exists, openForBooking is true, and now is not on the same day as departureTime.
Post-condition: Flight status is closed, and previously confirmed reservations are now canceled.

Airline::removeFlight
Summary: Removes a flight from the airline's system.
Algorithm: Locate flight in the flights list and remove it.
Related Features: flights (List)
Related Classes: Flight
Input: f (Flight): The flight to remove.
Output: void
Pre-condition: The flight exists in the airline's list.
Post-condition: Flight is removed from the airline's flight collection.

Airline::searchFlights
Summary: Searches for flights based on origin, destination, and date.
Algorithm: Iterate through flights list, filter by departureAirport, arrivalAirport, and check if departure date matches the provided date.
Related Features: flights (List)
Related Classes: Flight, EDate
Input: origin (String): ID of departure airport; dest (String): ID of arrival airport; date (EDate): Date of departure.
Output: List<Flight>: List of matching flights.
Pre-condition: None.
Post-condition: Returns a list of flights matching the criteria.

# Requirement
```text
Airlines offer different flights. Each flight has its unique id. A flight is open for booking and closed by order of the company. A customer can book one or more flights, for different passengers. A reservation concerns a single flight and a single passenger, has a unique id. A reservation can be confirmed or canceled. A flight has a departure airport and an arrival airport. Each airport has its unique id. A flight has a day and time of departure, and a day and time of arrival (e.g. 2024-12-08 13:00:00). A flight may include stopovers in one or more airport(s). A stopover has a departure time and an arrival time. Each airport serves one or more cities.
Functional requirement:
1.Publish a flight for booking. An airline can publish a newly created flight to make it available for customer bookings. The system first confirms that the flight has valid departure and arrival timestamps in yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss format, then checks temporal consistency — currentTime < departureTime < arrivalTime — and route integrity — departureAirport ≠ arrivalAirport. A flight may be published only once, and before publishing, the flight's openForBooking status must be false. The call returns true on success; otherwise, false.
2.Create a booking for passengers on a flight. A customer selects a specific open flight and supplies a list of passengers names. The system checks that there are no duplicate passengers on the flight and the current time is before the flight departure time. It then generates a booking for the customer and creates a reservation with a unique ID for each passenger in that booking. Each reservation is initially placed in "pending" status until the customer confirms it. The call returns true on success; otherwise, false.
3.Confirm or cancel an existing reservation in a booking. The system checks that the flight has not yet departed and is still open for booking. The customer can then confirm or cancel a reservation by providing its reservation ID. The call returns true on success; otherwise, false.
4.Close an open flight. An airline can close an existing flight that has not yet departed. The system verifies that the flight is currently open; if so, it changes the status to closed and cancels every confirmed reservation. Closing is not allowed on the same calendar day as the flight's departure — even if the current time is before the departure time. It returns true on success; otherwise, false.
5.Retrieve all confirmed reservations for a specific flight. Given a flight object, the system retrieves every confirmed reservation on that flight, provided the flight is currently open for booking. It returns a list of reservations, or empty list if none exist.
```

- The getter of a boolean attribute `bv` looks like `isBv()`, e.g., `isIsTrue()` for `isTrue`.
- When possibe, use the creation factory for object creation.
- To create an EList instance, import and use `org.eclipse.emf.common.util.BasicEList`.

## EMF Coding Style
- When possible, call getter/setter methods to access field values. Do not read/write raw fields derived from the class diagram.

```java
    // 3. Check if the passenger name already exists in any reservation associated with the flight.
    for (Reservation r : f.getReservations()) {
        if (r.getPassenger() != null && passengerName.equals(r.getPassenger().getName())) {
            return false;
        }
    }

    // 4. Create a new Reservation object with a unique ID, set status to PENDING, link to flight and passenger.
    Reservation newReservation = FlightsFactory.eINSTANCE.createReservation();
    newReservation.setId(UUID.randomUUID().toString());
    newReservation.setStatus(ReservationStatus.PENDING);
    newReservation.setFlight(f);

    Passenger passenger = FlightsFactory.eINSTANCE.createPassenger();
    passenger.setName(passengerName);
    newReservation.setPassenger(passenger);

    // 5. Add the reservation to this Booking's reservations list.
    this.getReservations().add(newReservation);

    // 6. Return true.
    return true;
  }
```

   * 1. Check if the flight is openForBooking.

   * 3. Check if the passenger name already exists in any reservation associated with the flight.
   * 4. Create a new Reservation object with a unique ID, set status to PENDING, link to flight and passenger.

   * 6. Return true.

   * Post-condition: If successful, a new Reservation with status PENDING is added to the booking's reservations list and the flight's reservations list.

   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"

    if (!f.isOpenForBooking()) {
        return false;

        return false;

You will be given a **Requirement** and a **Class Diagram** in PlantUML. Your task is to annotate every operation listed in **Operations** with a specification.

An operation specification must describe the following sections about the operation:
1. Summary: the summary of functionality;
2. Algorithm: algorithm or pseudo code;
3. Related Features: a list of structural or behavior features within this class that shall be accessed;
4. Related Classes: a list of classes and data types defined in **Class Diagram** that shall be accessed, in the format of `Related Classes: ClsA, CLsB, ...` or `Related Classes: None`;
5. Input: the input parameters, including the meaning, the format, and the value ranges if necessary;
6. Output: output value, including the meaning, the format, and the value ranges if necessary;
7. Pre-condition: the condition that the system and the input must satisfy before the operation is executed;
8. Post-condition: the condition that the system and the output must satisfy after the operation is executed.

Finish this task by following the guidelines below.
1. Take the principle of modularization into account.
2. For each operation, determine its functional boundary based on the given requirement. Ensure high cohesion and low coupling.
3. If there is any unspecified details, such as undefined constants, rates, and ratios, then you must infer them.
4. Make sure that all requirements can be covered.

# Requirement
```text
Airlines offer different flights. Each flight has its unique id. A flight is open for booking and closed by order of the company. A customer can book one or more flights, for different passengers. A reservation concerns a single flight and a single passenger, has a unique id. A reservation can be confirmed or canceled. A flight has a departure airport and an arrival airport. Each airport has its unique id. A flight has a day and time of departure, and a day and time of arrival (e.g. 2024-12-08 13:00:00). A flight may include stopovers in one or more airport(s). A stopover has a departure time and an arrival time. Each airport serves one or more cities.
Functional requirement:
1.Publish a flight for booking. An airline can publish a newly created flight to make it available for customer bookings. The system first confirms that the flight has valid departure and arrival timestamps in yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss format, then checks temporal consistency — currentTime < departureTime < arrivalTime — and route integrity — departureAirport ≠ arrivalAirport. A flight may be published only once, and before publishing, the flight's openForBooking status must be false. The call returns true on success; otherwise, false.
2.Create a booking for passengers on a flight. A customer selects a specific open flight and supplies a list of passengers names. The system checks that there are no duplicate passengers on the flight and the current time is before the flight departure time. It then generates a booking for the customer and creates a reservation with a unique ID for each passenger in that booking. Each reservation is initially placed in "pending" status until the customer confirms it. The call returns true on success; otherwise, false.
3.Confirm or cancel an existing reservation in a booking. The system checks that the flight has not yet departed and is still open for booking. The customer can then confirm or cancel a reservation by providing its reservation ID. The call returns true on success; otherwise, false.
4.Close an open flight. An airline can close an existing flight that has not yet departed. The system verifies that the flight is currently open; if so, it changes the status to closed and cancels every confirmed reservation. Closing is not allowed on the same calendar day as the flight's departure — even if the current time is before the departure time. It returns true on success; otherwise, false.
5.Retrieve all confirmed reservations for a specific flight. Given a flight object, the system retrieves every confirmed reservation on that flight, provided the flight is currently open for booking. It returns a list of reservations, or empty list if none exist.
```

# Class Diagram
```plantuml
@startuml

title flights Model

class Airline {
    flights : List<Flight>
    addFlight(f : Flight) : void
    closeFlight(flightId : String, now : EDate) : boolean
    publishFlight(f : Flight, now : EDate) : boolean
    removeFlight(f : Flight) : void
    searchFlights(origin : String, dest : String, date : EDate) : List<Flight>
}
class Airport {
    id : String
    servesForCities : List<City>
    addCity(c : City) : void
}
class Booking {
    customer : Customer
    reservations : List<Reservation>
    createReservation(f : Flight, passenger : String, now : EDate) : boolean
}
class City {
}
class Customer {
    bookings : List<Booking>
    addBooking(f : Flight, now : EDate, listOfPassengerNames : List<String>) : boolean
    cancel(reservationID : String, now : EDate) : boolean
    confirm(reservationID : String, now : EDate) : boolean
}
class Flight {
    arrivalTime : EDate
    departureTime : EDate
    id : String
    openForBooking : boolean
    arrivalAirport : Airport
    departureAirport : Airport
    reservations : List<Reservation>
    stopovers : List<Stopover>
    addStopover(stop : Stopover, now : EDate) : boolean
    getConfirmedReservations() : List<Reservation>
    removeStopover(stop : Stopover, now : EDate) : boolean
}
class Passenger {
    name : String
}
class Reservation {
    id : String
    status : ReservationStatus
    flight : Flight
    passenger : Passenger
}
class Stopover {
    arrivalTime : EDate
    departureTime : EDate
    airport : Airport
}
enum ReservationStatus {
    PENDING
    CONFIRMED
    CANCELED
}

Airline *-- "*" Flight : flights
Airport --> "*" City : servesForCities
Booking --> Customer : customer
Booking *-- "*" Reservation : reservations
Customer --> "*" Booking : bookings
Flight --> Airport : arrivalAirport
Flight --> Airport : departureAirport
Flight --> "*" Reservation : reservations  'opposite: flight
Flight *-- "*" Stopover : stopovers
Reservation --> Flight : flight  'opposite: reservations
Reservation --> Passenger : passenger
Stopover --> Airport : airport
@enduml
```

# Requirement
```text
Airlines offer different flights. Each flight has its unique id. A flight is open for booking and closed by order of the company. A customer can book one or more flights, for different passengers. A reservation concerns a single flight and a single passenger, has a unique id. A reservation can be confirmed or canceled. A flight has a departure airport and an arrival airport. Each airport has its unique id. A flight has a day and time of departure, and a day and time of arrival (e.g. 2024-12-08 13:00:00). A flight may include stopovers in one or more airport(s). A stopover has a departure time and an arrival time. Each airport serves one or more cities.
Functional requirement:
1.Publish a flight for booking. An airline can publish a newly created flight to make it available for customer bookings. The system first confirms that the flight has valid departure and arrival timestamps in yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss format, then checks temporal consistency — currentTime < departureTime < arrivalTime — and route integrity — departureAirport ≠ arrivalAirport. A flight may be published only once, and before publishing, the flight's openForBooking status must be false. The call returns true on success; otherwise, false.
2.Create a booking for passengers on a flight. A customer selects a specific open flight and supplies a list of passengers names. The system checks that there are no duplicate passengers on the flight and the current time is before the flight departure time. It then generates a booking for the customer and creates a reservation with a unique ID for each passenger in that booking. Each reservation is initially placed in "pending" status until the customer confirms it. The call returns true on success; otherwise, false.
3.Confirm or cancel an existing reservation in a booking. The system checks that the flight has not yet departed and is still open for booking. The customer can then confirm or cancel a reservation by providing its reservation ID. The call returns true on success; otherwise, false.
4.Close an open flight. An airline can close an existing flight that has not yet departed. The system verifies that the flight is currently open; if so, it changes the status to closed and cancels every confirmed reservation. Closing is not allowed on the same calendar day as the flight's departure — even if the current time is before the departure time. It returns true on success; otherwise, false.
5.Retrieve all confirmed reservations for a specific flight. Given a flight object, the system retrieves every confirmed reservation on that flight, provided the flight is currently open for booking. It returns a list of reservations, or empty list if none exist.
```

  res = find reservation by reservationID in customer's bookings.
  if res == null or not res.flight.openForBooking or now >= res.flight.departureTime, return false.
  res.status = CANCELED.
  return true.

# Requirement
```text
Airlines offer different flights. Each flight has its unique id. A flight is open for booking and closed by order of the company. A customer can book one or more flights, for different passengers. A reservation concerns a single flight and a single passenger, has a unique id. A reservation can be confirmed or canceled. A flight has a departure airport and an arrival airport. Each airport has its unique id. A flight has a day and time of departure, and a day and time of arrival (e.g. 2024-12-08 13:00:00). A flight may include stopovers in one or more airport(s). A stopover has a departure time and an arrival time. Each airport serves one or more cities.
Functional requirement:
1.Publish a flight for booking. An airline can publish a newly created flight to make it available for customer bookings. The system first confirms that the flight has valid departure and arrival timestamps in yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss format, then checks temporal consistency — currentTime < departureTime < arrivalTime — and route integrity — departureAirport ≠ arrivalAirport. A flight may be published only once, and before publishing, the flight's openForBooking status must be false. The call returns true on success; otherwise, false.
2.Create a booking for passengers on a flight. A customer selects a specific open flight and supplies a list of passengers names. The system checks that there are no duplicate passengers on the flight and the current time is before the flight departure time. It then generates a booking for the customer and creates a reservation with a unique ID for each passenger in that booking. Each reservation is initially placed in "pending" status until the customer confirms it. The call returns true on success; otherwise, false.
3.Confirm or cancel an existing reservation in a booking. The system checks that the flight has not yet departed and is still open for booking. The customer can then confirm or cancel a reservation by providing its reservation ID. The call returns true on success; otherwise, false.
4.Close an open flight. An airline can close an existing flight that has not yet departed. The system verifies that the flight is currently open; if so, it changes the status to closed and cancels every confirmed reservation. Closing is not allowed on the same calendar day as the flight's departure — even if the current time is before the departure time. It returns true on success; otherwise, false.
5.Retrieve all confirmed reservations for a specific flight. Given a flight object, the system retrieves every confirmed reservation on that flight, provided the flight is currently open for booking. It returns a list of reservations, or empty list if none exist.
```

# Requirement
```text
Airlines offer different flights. Each flight has its unique id. A flight is open for booking and closed by order of the company. A customer can book one or more flights, for different passengers. A reservation concerns a single flight and a single passenger, has a unique id. A reservation can be confirmed or canceled. A flight has a departure airport and an arrival airport. Each airport has its unique id. A flight has a day and time of departure, and a day and time of arrival (e.g. 2024-12-08 13:00:00). A flight may include stopovers in one or more airport(s). A stopover has a departure time and an arrival time. Each airport serves one or more cities.
Functional requirement:
1.Publish a flight for booking. An airline can publish a newly created flight to make it available for customer bookings. The system first confirms that the flight has valid departure and arrival timestamps in yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss format, then checks temporal consistency — currentTime < departureTime < arrivalTime — and route integrity — departureAirport ≠ arrivalAirport. A flight may be published only once, and before publishing, the flight's openForBooking status must be false. The call returns true on success; otherwise, false.
2.Create a booking for passengers on a flight. A customer selects a specific open flight and supplies a list of passengers names. The system checks that there are no duplicate passengers on the flight and the current time is before the flight departure time. It then generates a booking for the customer and creates a reservation with a unique ID for each passenger in that booking. Each reservation is initially placed in "pending" status until the customer confirms it. The call returns true on success; otherwise, false.
3.Confirm or cancel an existing reservation in a booking. The system checks that the flight has not yet departed and is still open for booking. The customer can then confirm or cancel a reservation by providing its reservation ID. The call returns true on success; otherwise, false.
4.Close an open flight. An airline can close an existing flight that has not yet departed. The system verifies that the flight is currently open; if so, it changes the status to closed and cancels every confirmed reservation. Closing is not allowed on the same calendar day as the flight's departure — even if the current time is before the departure time. It returns true on success; otherwise, false.
5.Retrieve all confirmed reservations for a specific flight. Given a flight object, the system retrieves every confirmed reservation on that flight, provided the flight is currently open for booking. It returns a list of reservations, or empty list if none exist.
```

# Requirement
```text
Airlines offer different flights. Each flight has its unique id. A flight is open for booking and closed by order of the company. A customer can book one or more flights, for different passengers. A reservation concerns a single flight and a single passenger, has a unique id. A reservation can be confirmed or canceled. A flight has a departure airport and an arrival airport. Each airport has its unique id. A flight has a day and time of departure, and a day and time of arrival (e.g. 2024-12-08 13:00:00). A flight may include stopovers in one or more airport(s). A stopover has a departure time and an arrival time. Each airport serves one or more cities.
Functional requirement:
1.Publish a flight for booking. An airline can publish a newly created flight to make it available for customer bookings. The system first confirms that the flight has valid departure and arrival timestamps in yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss format, then checks temporal consistency — currentTime < departureTime < arrivalTime — and route integrity — departureAirport ≠ arrivalAirport. A flight may be published only once, and before publishing, the flight's openForBooking status must be false. The call returns true on success; otherwise, false.
2.Create a booking for passengers on a flight. A customer selects a specific open flight and supplies a list of passengers names. The system checks that there are no duplicate passengers on the flight and the current time is before the flight departure time. It then generates a booking for the customer and creates a reservation with a unique ID for each passenger in that booking. Each reservation is initially placed in "pending" status until the customer confirms it. The call returns true on success; otherwise, false.
3.Confirm or cancel an existing reservation in a booking. The system checks that the flight has not yet departed and is still open for booking. The customer can then confirm or cancel a reservation by providing its reservation ID. The call returns true on success; otherwise, false.
4.Close an open flight. An airline can close an existing flight that has not yet departed. The system verifies that the flight is currently open; if so, it changes the status to closed and cancels every confirmed reservation. Closing is not allowed on the same calendar day as the flight's departure — even if the current time is before the departure time. It returns true on success; otherwise, false.
5.Retrieve all confirmed reservations for a specific flight. Given a flight object, the system retrieves every confirmed reservation on that flight, provided the flight is currently open for booking. It returns a list of reservations, or empty list if none exist.
```

Flight::removeStopover
Summary: Removes a stopover from the flight route.
Algorithm: Remove the stopover from the 'stopovers' list.
Related Features: stopovers
Related Classes: Stopover, EDate
Input: stop (Stopover), now (EDate).
Output: boolean: True if removed.
Pre-condition: Stopover exists in the list.
Post-condition: Stopover removed from flight.

Flight::addStopover
Summary: Adds a stopover to the flight route.
Algorithm: Append the stopover to the 'stopovers' list.
Related Features: stopovers
Related Classes: Stopover, EDate
Input: stop (Stopover), now (EDate).
Output: boolean: True if added.
Pre-condition: Stopover time is within flight departure/arrival window.
Post-condition: Stopover added to Flight.

Flight::getConfirmedReservations
Summary: Retrieves all confirmed reservations for the flight.
Algorithm:
  if not this.openForBooking, return empty list.
  return reservations.filter(r => r.status == CONFIRMED).
Related Features: reservations, status, openForBooking
Related Classes: Reservation, ReservationStatus
Input: None
Output: List<Reservation>: A list of confirmed reservations.
Pre-condition: The flight is open for booking.
Post-condition: Returns the list of confirmed reservations or an empty list.

# Operation Specifications
Airline::removeFlight
Summary: Removes a flight from the airline's management.
Algorithm: Remove the flight instance from the 'flights' list.
Related Features: flights
Related Classes: Flight
Input: f (Flight): The flight to remove.
Output: None
Pre-condition: f is in the flights list.
Post-condition: f is no longer in the flights list.

Airline::publishFlight
Summary: Publishes a created flight to make it available for customer bookings.
Algorithm: 
  if flight.openForBooking == true, return false.
  if flight.departureAirport == flight.arrivalAirport, return false.
  if not (now < flight.departureTime < flight.arrivalTime), return false.
  flight.openForBooking = true.
  return true.
Related Features: flights, openForBooking
Related Classes: Flight, EDate
Input: f (Flight): The flight to publish; now (EDate): The current system time.
Output: boolean: Returns true if the flight is successfully published, otherwise false.
Pre-condition: The flight exists and has valid departure/arrival timestamps.
Post-condition: The flight's openForBooking status is set to true if successful.

Airline::closeFlight
Summary: Closes an existing open flight.
Algorithm:
  f = find flight by flightId.
  if f == null or not f.openForBooking or (now.date == f.departureTime.date), return false.
  if now >= f.departureTime, return false.
  f.openForBooking = false.
  for each res in f.reservations:
    if res.status == CONFIRMED:
      res.status = CANCELED.
  return true.
Related Features: flights, openForBooking, reservations, status
Related Classes: Flight, Reservation, EDate
Input: flightId (String): The ID of the flight; now (EDate): The current time.
Output: boolean: Returns true if the flight is successfully closed, otherwise false.
Pre-condition: The flight is open and the current day is not the departure day.
Post-condition: The flight is closed and all confirmed reservations are canceled.

Airline::searchFlights
Summary: Search for flights by origin, destination, and date.
Algorithm: Filter the 'flights' list where departureAirport matches origin, arrivalAirport matches dest, and departure date matches the provided date.
Related Features: flights
Related Classes: Flight, Airport, EDate
Input: origin (String), dest (String), date (EDate).
Output: List<Flight>: List of matching flights.
Pre-condition: None.
Post-condition: Returns a list of flights matching criteria.

Airline::addFlight
Summary: Adds a new Flight object to the airline's management list.
Algorithm: Add the provided Flight instance to the internal 'flights' list.
Related Features: flights
Related Classes: Flight
Input: f (Flight): The flight object to be added.
Output: None
Pre-condition: f is not null and not already in the list.
Post-condition: The flight is contained within the airline's 'flights' list.

Airline::closeFlight
Summary: Closes an existing open flight.
Algorithm:
  f = find flight by flightId.
  if f == null or not f.openForBooking or (now.date == f.departureTime.date), return false.
  if now >= f.departureTime, return false.
  f.openForBooking = false.
  for each res in f.reservations:
    if res.status == CONFIRMED:
      res.status = CANCELED.
  return true.
Related Features: flights, openForBooking, reservations, status
Related Classes: Flight, Reservation, EDate
Input: flightId (String): The ID of the flight; now (EDate): The current time.
Output: boolean: Returns true if the flight is successfully closed, otherwise false.
Pre-condition: The flight is open and the current day is not the departure day.
Post-condition: The flight is closed and all confirmed reservations are canceled.

Airline::searchFlights
Summary: Search for flights by origin, destination, and date.
Algorithm: Filter the 'flights' list where departureAirport matches origin, arrivalAirport matches dest, and departure date matches the provided date.
Related Features: flights
Related Classes: Flight, Airport, EDate
Input: origin (String), dest (String), date (EDate).
Output: List<Flight>: List of matching flights.
Pre-condition: None.
Post-condition: Returns a list of flights matching criteria.

Airline::addFlight
Summary: Adds a new Flight object to the airline's management list.
Algorithm: Add the provided Flight instance to the internal 'flights' list.
Related Features: flights
Related Classes: Flight
Input: f (Flight): The flight object to be added.
Output: None
Pre-condition: f is not null and not already in the list.
Post-condition: The flight is contained within the airline's 'flights' list.

# Requirement
```text
Airlines offer different flights. Each flight has its unique id. A flight is open for booking and closed by order of the company. A customer can book one or more flights, for different passengers. A reservation concerns a single flight and a single passenger, has a unique id. A reservation can be confirmed or canceled. A flight has a departure airport and an arrival airport. Each airport has its unique id. A flight has a day and time of departure, and a day and time of arrival (e.g. 2024-12-08 13:00:00). A flight may include stopovers in one or more airport(s). A stopover has a departure time and an arrival time. Each airport serves one or more cities.
Functional requirement:
1.Publish a flight for booking. An airline can publish a newly created flight to make it available for customer bookings. The system first confirms that the flight has valid departure and arrival timestamps in yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss format, then checks temporal consistency — currentTime < departureTime < arrivalTime — and route integrity — departureAirport ≠ arrivalAirport. A flight may be published only once, and before publishing, the flight's openForBooking status must be false. The call returns true on success; otherwise, false.
2.Create a booking for passengers on a flight. A customer selects a specific open flight and supplies a list of passengers names. The system checks that there are no duplicate passengers on the flight and the current time is before the flight departure time. It then generates a booking for the customer and creates a reservation with a unique ID for each passenger in that booking. Each reservation is initially placed in "pending" status until the customer confirms it. The call returns true on success; otherwise, false.
3.Confirm or cancel an existing reservation in a booking. The system checks that the flight has not yet departed and is still open for booking. The customer can then confirm or cancel a reservation by providing its reservation ID. The call returns true on success; otherwise, false.
4.Close an open flight. An airline can close an existing flight that has not yet departed. The system verifies that the flight is currently open; if so, it changes the status to closed and cancels every confirmed reservation. Closing is not allowed on the same calendar day as the flight's departure — even if the current time is before the departure time. It returns true on success; otherwise, false.
5.Retrieve all confirmed reservations for a specific flight. Given a flight object, the system retrieves every confirmed reservation on that flight, provided the flight is currently open for booking. It returns a list of reservations, or empty list if none exist.
```

- The getter of a boolean attribute `bv` looks like `isBv()`, e.g., `isIsTrue()` for `isTrue`.
- When possibe, use the creation factory for object creation.
- To create an EList instance, import and use `org.eclipse.emf.common.util.BasicEList`.

      for (Reservation r : b.getReservations()) {
        if (reservationID.equals(r.getId())) {
          res = r;
          break;
        }
      }
      if (res != null) break;
    }

    if (res == null || !res.getFlight().isOpenForBooking() || now.compareTo(res.getFlight().getDepartureTime()) >= 0) {
      return false;
    }

    res.setStatus(ReservationStatus.CANCELED);
    return true;
  }

  @Override
  public Object eGet(int featureID, boolean resolve, boolean coreType)
  {
    switch (featureID)
    {
      case FlightsPackage.CUSTOMER__BOOKINGS:
        return getBookings();
    }
    return super.eGet(featureID, resolve, coreType);
  }

  @SuppressWarnings("unchecked")
  @Override
  public void eSet(int featureID, Object newValue)
  {
    switch (featureID)
    {
      case FlightsPackage.CUSTOMER__BOOKINGS:
        getBookings().clear();
        getBookings().addAll((Collection<? extends Booking>)newValue);
        return;
    }
    super.eSet(featureID, newValue);
  }

  @Override
  public void eUnset(int featureID)
  {
    switch (featureID)
    {
      case FlightsPackage.CUSTOMER__BOOKINGS:
        getBookings().clear();
        return;
    }
    super.eUnset(featureID);
  }

  @Override
  public boolean eIsSet(int featureID)
  {
    switch (featureID)
    {
      case FlightsPackage.CUSTOMER__BOOKINGS:
        return bookings != null && !bookings.isEmpty();
    }
    return super.eIsSet(featureID);
  }

- To create an EList instance, import and use `org.eclipse.emf.common.util.BasicEList`.

## EMF Coding Style
- When possible, call getter/setter methods to access field values. Do not read/write raw fields derived from the class diagram.
- The getter of a boolean attribute `bv` looks like `isBv()`, e.g., `isIsTrue()` for `isTrue`.
- When possibe, use the creation factory for object creation.
- To create an EList instance, import and use `org.eclipse.emf.common.util.BasicEList`.

# Requirement
```text
Airlines offer different flights. Each flight has its unique id. A flight is open for booking and closed by order of the company. A customer can book one or more flights, for different passengers. A reservation concerns a single flight and a single passenger, has a unique id. A reservation can be confirmed or canceled. A flight has a departure airport and an arrival airport. Each airport has its unique id. A flight has a day and time of departure, and a day and time of arrival (e.g. 2024-12-08 13:00:00). A flight may include stopovers in one or more airport(s). A stopover has a departure time and an arrival time. Each airport serves one or more cities.
Functional requirement:
1.Publish a flight for booking. An airline can publish a newly created flight to make it available for customer bookings. The system first confirms that the flight has valid departure and arrival timestamps in yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss format, then checks temporal consistency — currentTime < departureTime < arrivalTime — and route integrity — departureAirport ≠ arrivalAirport. A flight may be published only once, and before publishing, the flight's openForBooking status must be false. The call returns true on success; otherwise, false.
2.Create a booking for passengers on a flight. A customer selects a specific open flight and supplies a list of passengers names. The system checks that there are no duplicate passengers on the flight and the current time is before the flight departure time. It then generates a booking for the customer and creates a reservation with a unique ID for each passenger in that booking. Each reservation is initially placed in "pending" status until the customer confirms it. The call returns true on success; otherwise, false.
3.Confirm or cancel an existing reservation in a booking. The system checks that the flight has not yet departed and is still open for booking. The customer can then confirm or cancel a reservation by providing its reservation ID. The call returns true on success; otherwise, false.
4.Close an open flight. An airline can close an existing flight that has not yet departed. The system verifies that the flight is currently open; if so, it changes the status to closed and cancels every confirmed reservation. Closing is not allowed on the same calendar day as the flight's departure — even if the current time is before the departure time. It returns true on success; otherwise, false.
5.Retrieve all confirmed reservations for a specific flight. Given a flight object, the system retrieves every confirmed reservation on that flight, provided the flight is currently open for booking. It returns a list of reservations, or empty list if none exist.
```

# Class Diagram
```plantuml
@startuml

title flights Model

class Airline {
    flights : List<Flight>
    addFlight(f : Flight) : void
    closeFlight(flightId : String, now : EDate) : boolean
    publishFlight(f : Flight, now : EDate) : boolean
    removeFlight(f : Flight) : void
    searchFlights(origin : String, dest : String, date : EDate) : List<Flight>
}
class Airport {
    id : String
    servesForCities : List<City>
    addCity(c : City) : void
}
class Booking {
    customer : Customer
    reservations : List<Reservation>
    createReservation(f : Flight, passenger : String, now : EDate) : boolean
}
class City {
}
class Customer {
    bookings : List<Booking>
    addBooking(f : Flight, now : EDate, listOfPassengerNames : List<String>) : boolean
    cancel(reservationID : String, now : EDate) : boolean
    confirm(reservationID : String, now : EDate) : boolean
}
class Flight {
    arrivalTime : EDate
    departureTime : EDate
    id : String
    openForBooking : boolean
    arrivalAirport : Airport
    departureAirport : Airport
    reservations : List<Reservation>
    stopovers : List<Stopover>
    addStopover(stop : Stopover, now : EDate) : boolean
    getConfirmedReservations() : List<Reservation>
    removeStopover(stop : Stopover, now : EDate) : boolean
}
class Passenger {
    name : String
}
class Reservation {
    id : String
    status : ReservationStatus
    flight : Flight
    passenger : Passenger
}
class Stopover {
    arrivalTime : EDate
    departureTime : EDate
    airport : Airport
}
enum ReservationStatus {
    PENDING
    CONFIRMED
    CANCELED
}

Airline *-- "*" Flight : flights
Airport --> "*" City : servesForCities
Booking --> Customer : customer
Booking *-- "*" Reservation : reservations
Customer --> "*" Booking : bookings
Flight --> Airport : arrivalAirport
Flight --> Airport : departureAirport
Flight --> "*" Reservation : reservations  'opposite: flight
Flight *-- "*" Stopover : stopovers
Reservation --> Flight : flight  'opposite: reservations
Reservation --> Passenger : passenger
Stopover --> Airport : airport
@enduml
```

```plantuml
    addFlight(f : Flight) : void
    closeFlight(flightId : String, now : EDate) : boolean
    publishFlight(f : Flight, now : EDate) : boolean
    removeFlight(f : Flight) : void
    searchFlights(origin : String, dest : String, date : EDate) : List<Flight>

    id : String
    servesForCities : List<City>

    createReservation(f : Flight, passenger : String, now : EDate) : boolean

}

    bookings : List<Booking>
    addBooking(f : Flight, now : EDate, listOfPassengerNames : List<String>) : boolean
    cancel(reservationID : String, now : EDate) : boolean
    confirm(reservationID : String, now : EDate) : boolean
}
class Flight {
    arrivalTime : EDate
    departureTime : EDate
    id : String
    openForBooking : boolean
    arrivalAirport : Airport
    departureAirport : Airport
    reservations : List<Reservation>
    stopovers : List<Stopover>
    addStopover(stop : Stopover, now : EDate) : boolean
    getConfirmedReservations() : List<Reservation>
    removeStopover(stop : Stopover, now : EDate) : boolean
}
class Passenger {
    name : String
}

    id : String
    status : ReservationStatus
    flight : Flight
    passenger : Passenger
}

    arrivalTime : EDate
    departureTime : EDate

}

    PENDING
    CONFIRMED
    CANCELED

Flight --> Airport : arrivalAirport

Stopover --> Airport : airport
@enduml
```

# Operation Specifications
Airline::publishFlight
Summary: Publishes a flight to make it available for booking.
Algorithm: Validate timestamps (departure < arrival); validate route (departureAirport != arrivalAirport); verify flight is not already open; set openForBooking to true.
Related Features: flights, Flight::openForBooking, Flight::departureTime, Flight::arrivalTime
Related Classes: Flight, EDate
Input: f: Flight, now: EDate
Output: boolean (true if success, false if validation fails)
Pre-condition: Flight exists, openForBooking is false, currentTime < departureTime.
Post-condition: Flight openForBooking is true.

Airline::addFlight
Summary: Adds a new Flight instance to the airline's management list.
Algorithm: Check if flight exists; if not, add to the flights list.
Related Features: flights (List<Flight>)
Related Classes: Flight
Input: f: Flight (the flight object to add)
Output: None
Pre-condition: f is not null and not already in the list.
Post-condition: The flight is contained in the airline's flights list.

Airline::closeFlight
Summary: Closes a flight for booking and cancels all confirmed reservations.
Algorithm: Find flight by ID; check if openForBooking is true and current date is not the same as departure date; set openForBooking to false; iterate through reservations and set status to CANCELED if currently CONFIRMED.
Related Features: flights, Flight::openForBooking, Flight::reservations
Related Classes: Flight, Reservation, ReservationStatus, EDate
Input: flightId: String (unique ID), now: EDate (current system time)
Output: boolean (true if successful, false otherwise)
Pre-condition: Flight exists; flight has not departed.
Post-condition: Flight's openForBooking is false; all previous CONFIRMED reservations are CANCELED.

Airline::searchFlights
Summary: Searches for flights by route and date.
Algorithm: Filter the flights list matching origin, destination, and date criteria.
Related Features: flights, Flight::departureAirport, Flight::arrivalAirport
Related Classes: Flight, Airport, EDate
Input: origin: String, dest: String, date: EDate
Output: List<Flight>
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: Returns a list of flights matching the criteria.

Airline::removeFlight
Summary: Removes a flight from the airline's record.
Algorithm: Find flight in list and remove it.
Related Features: flights
Related Classes: Flight
Input: f: Flight
Output: None
Pre-condition: Flight exists in the airline's list.
Post-condition: Flight is no longer in the flights list.

# Requirement
```text
Airlines offer different flights. Each flight has its unique id. A flight is open for booking and closed by order of the company. A customer can book one or more flights, for different passengers. A reservation concerns a single flight and a single passenger, has a unique id. A reservation can be confirmed or canceled. A flight has a departure airport and an arrival airport. Each airport has its unique id. A flight has a day and time of departure, and a day and time of arrival (e.g. 2024-12-08 13:00:00). A flight may include stopovers in one or more airport(s). A stopover has a departure time and an arrival time. Each airport serves one or more cities.
Functional requirement:
1.Publish a flight for booking. An airline can publish a newly created flight to make it available for customer bookings. The system first confirms that the flight has valid departure and arrival timestamps in yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss format, then checks temporal consistency — currentTime < departureTime < arrivalTime — and route integrity — departureAirport ≠ arrivalAirport. A flight may be published only once, and before publishing, the flight's openForBooking status must be false. The call returns true on success; otherwise, false.
2.Create a booking for passengers on a flight. A customer selects a specific open flight and supplies a list of passengers names. The system checks that there are no duplicate passengers on the flight and the current time is before the flight departure time. It then generates a booking for the customer and creates a reservation with a unique ID for each passenger in that booking. Each reservation is initially placed in "pending" status until the customer confirms it. The call returns true on success; otherwise, false.
3.Confirm or cancel an existing reservation in a booking. The system checks that the flight has not yet departed and is still open for booking. The customer can then confirm or cancel a reservation by providing its reservation ID. The call returns true on success; otherwise, false.
4.Close an open flight. An airline can close an existing flight that has not yet departed. The system verifies that the flight is currently open; if so, it changes the status to closed and cancels every confirmed reservation. Closing is not allowed on the same calendar day as the flight's departure — even if the current time is before the departure time. It returns true on success; otherwise, false.
5.Retrieve all confirmed reservations for a specific flight. Given a flight object, the system retrieves every confirmed reservation on that flight, provided the flight is currently open for booking. It returns a list of reservations, or empty list if none exist.
```

Customer::cancel
Summary: Cancels an existing reservation.
Algorithm: Find reservation by ID; verify flight not departed and is open; change status to CANCELED.
Related Features: bookings, Reservation::status
Related Classes: Reservation, EDate, ReservationStatus
Input: reservationID: String, now: EDate
Output: boolean (true if successful)
Pre-condition: Reservation exists and is CONFIRMED or PENDING.
Post-condition: Reservation status is CANCELED.

Customer::confirm
Summary: Confirms a pending reservation.
Algorithm: Find reservation by ID; verify flight not departed and is open; change status to CONFIRMED.
Related Features: bookings, Reservation::status
Related Classes: Reservation, EDate, ReservationStatus
Input: reservationID: String, now: EDate
Output: boolean (true if successful)
Pre-condition: Reservation exists and is PENDING.
Post-condition: Reservation status is CONFIRMED.

Customer::addBooking
Summary: Creates a booking with multiple passengers for a flight.
Algorithm: Verify flight is open; check no duplicate passengers; for each name, call createReservation; add booking to customer list.
Related Features: bookings, Booking::reservations
Related Classes: Flight, Booking, EDate
Input: f: Flight, now: EDate, listOfPassengerNames: List<String>
Output: boolean (true if successful)
Pre-condition: Flight is open and departure time is in the future.
Post-condition: A new booking is created with reservations for all passengers.

Customer::cancel

Related Features: bookings, Reservation::status

Pre-condition: Reservation exists and is CONFIRMED or PENDING.
Post-condition: Reservation status is CANCELED.

Customer::confirm
Summary: Confirms a pending reservation.
Algorithm: Find reservation by ID; verify flight not departed and is open; change status to CONFIRMED.
Related Features: bookings, Reservation::status
Related Classes: Reservation, EDate, ReservationStatus
Input: reservationID: String, now: EDate
Output: boolean (true if successful)
Pre-condition: Reservation exists and is PENDING.
Post-condition: Reservation status is CONFIRMED.

Customer::addBooking
Summary: Creates a booking with multiple passengers for a flight.
Algorithm: Verify flight is open; check no duplicate passengers; for each name, call createReservation; add booking to customer list.
Related Features: bookings, Booking::reservations
Related Classes: Flight, Booking, EDate
Input: f: Flight, now: EDate, listOfPassengerNames: List<String>
Output: boolean (true if successful)
Pre-condition: Flight is open and departure time is in the future.
Post-condition: A new booking is created with reservations for all passengers.

# Requirement
```text
Airlines offer different flights. Each flight has its unique id. A flight is open for booking and closed by order of the company. A customer can book one or more flights, for different passengers. A reservation concerns a single flight and a single passenger, has a unique id. A reservation can be confirmed or canceled. A flight has a departure airport and an arrival airport. Each airport has its unique id. A flight has a day and time of departure, and a day and time of arrival (e.g. 2024-12-08 13:00:00). A flight may include stopovers in one or more airport(s). A stopover has a departure time and an arrival time. Each airport serves one or more cities.
Functional requirement:
1.Publish a flight for booking. An airline can publish a newly created flight to make it available for customer bookings. The system first confirms that the flight has valid departure and arrival timestamps in yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss format, then checks temporal consistency — currentTime < departureTime < arrivalTime — and route integrity — departureAirport ≠ arrivalAirport. A flight may be published only once, and before publishing, the flight's openForBooking status must be false. The call returns true on success; otherwise, false.
2.Create a booking for passengers on a flight. A customer selects a specific open flight and supplies a list of passengers names. The system checks that there are no duplicate passengers on the flight and the current time is before the flight departure time. It then generates a booking for the customer and creates a reservation with a unique ID for each passenger in that booking. Each reservation is initially placed in "pending" status until the customer confirms it. The call returns true on success; otherwise, false.
3.Confirm or cancel an existing reservation in a booking. The system checks that the flight has not yet departed and is still open for booking. The customer can then confirm or cancel a reservation by providing its reservation ID. The call returns true on success; otherwise, false.
4.Close an open flight. An airline can close an existing flight that has not yet departed. The system verifies that the flight is currently open; if so, it changes the status to closed and cancels every confirmed reservation. Closing is not allowed on the same calendar day as the flight's departure — even if the current time is before the departure time. It returns true on success; otherwise, false.
5.Retrieve all confirmed reservations for a specific flight. Given a flight object, the system retrieves every confirmed reservation on that flight, provided the flight is currently open for booking. It returns a list of reservations, or empty list if none exist.
```

# Requirement
```text
Airlines offer different flights. Each flight has its unique id. A flight is open for booking and closed by order of the company. A customer can book one or more flights, for different passengers. A reservation concerns a single flight and a single passenger, has a unique id. A reservation can be confirmed or canceled. A flight has a departure airport and an arrival airport. Each airport has its unique id. A flight has a day and time of departure, and a day and time of arrival (e.g. 2024-12-08 13:00:00). A flight may include stopovers in one or more airport(s). A stopover has a departure time and an arrival time. Each airport serves one or more cities.
Functional requirement:
1.Publish a flight for booking. An airline can publish a newly created flight to make it available for customer bookings. The system first confirms that the flight has valid departure and arrival timestamps in yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss format, then checks temporal consistency — currentTime < departureTime < arrivalTime — and route integrity — departureAirport ≠ arrivalAirport. A flight may be published only once, and before publishing, the flight's openForBooking status must be false. The call returns true on success; otherwise, false.
2.Create a booking for passengers on a flight. A customer selects a specific open flight and supplies a list of passengers names. The system checks that there are no duplicate passengers on the flight and the current time is before the flight departure time. It then generates a booking for the customer and creates a reservation with a unique ID for each passenger in that booking. Each reservation is initially placed in "pending" status until the customer confirms it. The call returns true on success; otherwise, false.
3.Confirm or cancel an existing reservation in a booking. The system checks that the flight has not yet departed and is still open for booking. The customer can then confirm or cancel a reservation by providing its reservation ID. The call returns true on success; otherwise, false.
4.Close an open flight. An airline can close an existing flight that has not yet departed. The system verifies that the flight is currently open; if so, it changes the status to closed and cancels every confirmed reservation. Closing is not allowed on the same calendar day as the flight's departure — even if the current time is before the departure time. It returns true on success; otherwise, false.
5.Retrieve all confirmed reservations for a specific flight. Given a flight object, the system retrieves every confirmed reservation on that flight, provided the flight is currently open for booking. It returns a list of reservations, or empty list if none exist.
```

   * Algorithm: Validate that the stopover's arrival time is before its departure time and that these times are consistent with the flight's overall departure and arrival times. Add the stopover to the stopovers list. Return true if successful, false otherwise.
   * Related Features: stopovers, departureTime, arrivalTime
   * Related Classes: Stopover, EDate
   * Input: stop: Stopover, now: EDate
   * Output: boolean (true if successful, false otherwise)
   * Pre-condition: The stopover object is not null and the timing is consistent with the flight schedule.
   * Post-condition: The stopover is added to the flight's stopovers list if validation passes.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public boolean addStopover(final Stopover stop, final Date now)
  {
    if (stop == null) return false;
    
    Date stopArrival = stop.getArrivalTime();
    Date stopDeparture = stop.getDepartureTime();
    
    // Validate arrival before departure
    if (stopArrival == null || stopDeparture == null || stopArrival.after(stopDeparture)) {
        return false;
    }
    
    // Validate consistency with flight schedule
    Date flightDeparture = this.getDepartureTime();
    Date flightArrival = this.getArrivalTime();
    
    if (flightDeparture == null || flightArrival == null) return false;
    
    if (stopArrival.before(flightDeparture) || stopDeparture.after(flightArrival)) {
        return false;
    }
    
    return getStopovers().add(stop);
  }

  /**
   * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
   * <!-- end-user-doc -->
   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
```java
   * Summary: Creates a new reservation for a passenger on a specific flight.
   * Algorithm: 
   *   1. Check if the flight is open for booking and if the current time is before the departure time.
   *   2. Check if the passenger name already exists in the flight's current reservations list.
   *   3. If valid, create a new Reservation object with a unique ID, status PENDING, and link it to the flight and passenger.
   *   4. Add the reservation to the Booking's reservations list and the Flight's reservations list.
   *   5. Return true.
   * Related Features: reservations, Booking::customer, Flight::reservations
   * Related Classes: Flight, Reservation, ReservationStatus, EDate, Passenger
   * Input: f: Flight, passenger: String, now: EDate
   * Output: boolean (true if created successfully, false otherwise)
   * Pre-condition: Flight exists and is currently marked as openForBooking, and now < f.departureTime.
   * Post-condition: A new PENDING reservation is associated with the flight and added to the booking, or the operation returns false.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
```
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public boolean createReservation(final Flight f, final String passengerName, final Date now)
  {
    // 1. Check if the flight is open for booking and if the current time is before the departure time.
    if (f == null || !f.isOpenForBooking() || (f.getDepartureTime() != null && !now.before(f.getDepartureTime()))) {
        return false;
    }

    // 2. Check if the passenger name already exists in the flight's current reservations list.
    for (Reservation r : f.getReservations()) {
        if (r.getPassenger() != null && passengerName.equals(r.getPassenger().getName())) {
            return false;
        }
    }

    // 3. If valid, create a new Reservation object with a unique ID, status PENDING, and link it to the flight and passenger.
    Reservation newReservation = FlightsFactory.eINSTANCE.createReservation();
    newReservation.setId(UUID.randomUUID().toString());
    newReservation.setStatus(ReservationStatus.PENDING);
    newReservation.setFlight(f);
    
    Passenger passenger = FlightsFactory.eINSTANCE.createPassenger();
    passenger.setName(passengerName);
    newReservation.setPassenger(passenger);

    // 4. Add the reservation to the Booking's reservations list and the Flight's reservations list.
    this.getReservations().add(newReservation);
    f.getReservations().add(newReservation);

    // 5. Return true.
    return true;
  }

## EMF Coding Style
- When possible, call getter/setter methods to access field values. Do not read/write raw fields derived from the class diagram.

   * Related Classes: Flight, Reservation, ReservationStatus, EDate, Passenger
   * Input: f: Flight, passenger: String, now: EDate
   * Output: boolean (true if created successfully, false otherwise)
   * Pre-condition: Flight exists and is currently marked as openForBooking, and now < f.departureTime.
   * Post-condition: A new PENDING reservation is associated with the flight and added to the booking, or the operation returns false.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public boolean createReservation(final Flight f, final String passengerName, final Date now)
  {
    // 1. Check if the flight is open for booking and if the current time is before the departure time.
    if (f == null || !f.isOpenForBooking() || (f.getDepartureTime() != null && !now.before(f.getDepartureTime()))) {
        return false;
    }

    // 2. Check if the passenger name already exists in the flight's current reservations list.
    for (Reservation r : f.getReservations()) {
        if (r.getPassenger() != null && passengerName.equals(r.getPassenger().getName())) {
            return false;
        }
    }

    // 3. If valid, create a new Reservation object with a unique ID, status PENDING, and link it to the flight and passenger.
    Reservation newReservation = FlightsFactory.eINSTANCE.createReservation();
    newReservation.setId(UUID.randomUUID().toString());
    newReservation.setStatus(ReservationStatus.PENDING);
    newReservation.setFlight(f);
    
    Passenger newPassenger = FlightsFactory.eINSTANCE.createPassenger();
    newPassenger.setName(passengerName);
    newReservation.setPassenger(newPassenger);

    // 4. Add the reservation to the Booking's reservations list and the Flight's reservations list.
    this.getReservations().add(newReservation);
    f.getReservations().add(newReservation);

    // 5. Return true.
    return true;
  }
